chunks: Three narrated from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abi Basir, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and do righteous deeds, but He grants him authority over those who take Satan as a guardian instead of Allah and take the believers as enemies; those are the ones who have gone astray from the path.

He said: And this hadith is in the book Al-Tawhid by Al-Saduq (may Allah have mercy on him), and we counted it in this book, and it is from one of the hadiths we mention in the chapter of the Unity of Allah and His attributes.
ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Saduq's *Al-Tawhid* features Ibn Abbas and Imam al-Husayn (AS) responding to the Kharijite Nafi' ibn al-Azraq, who challenged their theological depth by contrasting it with the triviality of ruling on small insects. Imam al-Husayn articulates a profound Shia doctrine of divine unity (*Tawhid*), emphasizing that God is known by His own description, transcending human senses and analogy (*Qiyas*), thereby refuting anthropomorphism and establishing the Ahl al-Bayt as the true inheritors of divine knowledge.
